title: Build a Promo Code System in Python (Checkout Tutorial, Part 3)
creator: Leo Tanaka
description:
Part 3 of the Pixel Pantry series: we add discount codes to our fake grocery store's checkout. Expiry dates, minimum orders, one use per customer, and the bug that every real shop has shipped at least once.

Repo for the series: github.com/leotanaka/pixel-pantry (branch part-3)

0:00 Recap
0:40 The data model
1:50 Validating a code
3:00 Stacking bug
4:10 Tests

sentences.t: Welcome back to part three of the Pixel Pantry series, where we're building a grocery store checkout from scratch.
Last time we got the cart working, and today we're adding the thing every shop eventually needs, discount codes.
If you're just joining, Pixel Pantry is a fake store, it doesn't exist, it's just our practice project.
Okay, let's open up the models file and make a new dataclass for a promo code.
It needs a code string, a percent off, an expiry date, a minimum order total, and a flag for single use.
I'm storing the percent as an integer, twenty means twenty percent, because floats and money do not mix.
Now, before we write the logic, I want a realistic example to test against, so picture the banner on our homepage.
It says, new customers, use code SAVE20 for twenty percent off your first order over thirty dollars.
Free delivery this week only, offer ends Sunday.
That one sentence is actually four rules, and that's what we have to turn into code.
New customers only, so we need to check the order history, and over thirty dollars is the minimum total.
First order means single use, and ends Sunday is our expiry date, so let's write all four.
So I'll make a function called apply code, and it takes the cart, the customer, and whatever they typed in the box.
First line, strip the whitespace and uppercase it, because people will absolutely type save twenty with a space at the end.
Then we look it up in a dictionary, and if it's not there we return the cart unchanged with an error message.
Next, expiry, compare today's date with the expiry date, and if we're past it, same thing, error out.
Then the minimum, we sum the cart before any discount and check it against the minimum total.
And single use, we look in the customer's past orders to see if this code was already applied.
Let's run it.
Thirty five dollar cart, new customer, and we get twenty eight dollars, which is correct, nice.
Now here's the bug I promised you, the one that real shops have actually shipped.
What happens if I apply the code, then remove items so the cart drops under thirty?
Look at that, the discount stays on, because we only checked the minimum at the moment the code was applied.
So someone could buy one banana for eighty cents off, which, okay, not a huge deal, but scale that up.
The fix is to never store the discounted price, store the code, and recompute the total every single time the cart changes.
Now the stacking problem, what if someone has two codes?
Our rule is going to be one code per order, and the last one typed replaces the first one.
Some stores let you stack, and if you ever build that, apply percentages before flat amounts, or you'll give away money.
Alright, tests, because I am not shipping a money feature without tests.
Expired code, rejected, below minimum, rejected, second use, rejected, lowercase with spaces, accepted.
And the banana test, cart drops under thirty after applying, discount disappears, perfect.
All green, let's commit that, the branch is called part three if you're following along.
Next time we'll hook this up to a real payment sandbox, which is where things get scary.
If you got stuck anywhere, drop the error in the comments and I'll try to help, see you in part four.
